title: China $17 mn Mongla factory: Can Bangladesh move up the apparel chain?
content:
Longteng has signed an agreement for a planned $17 million intimate-apparel factory at Bangladesh’s Mongla EPZ, widening Bangladesh’s higher-value apparel base.
BEPZA projects six million pieces a year and about 3,005 jobs, though output, employment and buyer orders are not confirmed.
Section 301 duties put covered Bangladeshi goods at 10 per cent, below 12.5 per cent for China and Vietnam.

title: Indonesia’s 2027 tariff cliff: Can CEPA protect apparel and footwear?
content:
Indonesia will leave the EU’s GSP on January 1, 2027, creating a potential tariff gap if CEPA is not in force.
The EU and Indonesia finalised CEPA talks on September 23, 2025; it remained unsigned on October 14, with consent and internal procedures still ahead.
Exporters and EU buyers should model GSP and standard-duty scenarios, confirm tariff codes and rules of origin before 2027 shipments.

title: India-US trade pact's first tranche finalised: Piyush Goyal
content:
The first phase of the India-US bilateral trade agreement has been finalised and is undergoing legal drafting, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said. 
India aims to secure competitive tariff advantages before operationalising the pact. 
Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said negotiations were progressing positively, while the agreement's signing depends on the broader US tariff framework.

title: North Indian cotton yarn sees mixed trend as raw cotton firms up
content:
North India’s cotton yarn market was mixed, with Ludhiana up ₹5 (~$0.05) per kg on stronger cotton prices and better buying, while Delhi stayed largely steady amid weak consumer demand and payment constraints.
Panipat recycled yarn fell ₹2–4 per kg as sluggish export demand weighed on recycled PC yarn.
Raw cotton firmed by ₹10–20 per maund as arrivals slowed and mills bought consistently.

title: Why India's trade deficit with China widening despite export growth?
content:
India's trade deficit with China widened 20.7 per cent to $105.93 billion during January–September, despite Indian exports surging 40.7 per cent to $19.26 billion. 
Chinese exports to India rose 23.3 per cent to $125.19 billion, taking bilateral trade to $144.45 billion. 
The deficit approached 2025's record $116.12 billion, reflecting continued dependence on Chinese machinery and industrial inputs.

title: ICE cotton futures rise slightly but fail to sustain early gains
content:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled 15 points higher at 80.66 cents per pound after a rally to 82.25 cents faded as US inflation lifted the dollar.
Weak exports, higher USDA production and ending-stock estimates, and a 31 per cent US harvest kept the market range-bound.
Crop concerns and limited farmer selling offered support as traders track the dollar, Federal Reserve rates, exports and harvest.

title: Bangladesh non-cotton garment exports reach 30.7% share in Jan-Sep
content:
Bangladesh’s non-cotton garments took a 30.7 per cent share of total garment exports in January-September 2026, as demand from international clothing retailers and brands rose, according to the Export Promotion Bureau data. 
Total garment exports stood at $29.91 billion, with cotton at $20.75 billion and non-cotton at $9.17 billion. 
The non-cotton share peaked at 34.6 per cent in August.

title: Bangladesh's RMG exports to non-traditional markets rise 9.4% in Q1
content:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports to non-traditional markets rose 9.40 per cent to $1.81 billion in July-September FY26-27, outpacing EU growth. 
Shipments to five leading destinations increased 9.62 per cent to $1.03 billion. 
Turkiye drove about 90 per cent of their combined increase, while Japan remained the largest destination. India was the only market among the five to record a quarterly decline.

title: US apparel unit values jump 7.2%: Are Asian factories paid more?
content:
US apparel imports dropped by nearly $4 billion in January-July 2026, with China and India accounting for almost 83 per cent of the net decline.
OTEXA-based data show January-August imports at about $49.08 billion, down 7.42 per cent, while volumes fell 8.98 per cent.
Cambodia gained shipments, Bangladesh rose in August and Vietnam lifted share, but Asian average unit values mostly weakened.
